newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was generally lower on mostly moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings, USDA said.

Retail and HRI demand was for immediate needs, while forward interest was light. Even as slaughter levels remain light, inventories on rib, round, and loin cuts were quite a burden as demand, both domestic and export, has not lent the needed support. Therefore, these cuts trended lower throughout the trading period, with the middle meats experiencing the biggest losses.

After two weeks' of heavy discounting, chuck cuts managed to trade at generally steady levels. Some chuck cuts, such as the 2-piece boneless, traded higher early in the week and then stabilized by midweek. Inventories on these cuts were more manageable, compared to the previous period, as grinder's entered the market early in the week to fill some of their grinding needs.
Closely trimmed items also traded lower on fairly light demand as retailers saw no additional value on these cuts. Trade on beef trimmings started the week with just a few trades at steady levels.

As the week progressed, a weak undertone prevailed as demand was light and offerings were mostly moderate. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 3.00 to 7.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to 1.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 1.50 to 2.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 3.00 to 5.00 lower; Closely trimmed item's 2.00 lower; Beef trimmings 1.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 2.00 at 101.30; 700/850 Dn 2.26 at 100.44; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.78 at 96.03; 700/850 Dn 1.99 at 95.12.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The lean boneless beef declined after last week's gains, despite upward trending live cow prices in many areas. However, a firm undertone was noted at week's end as supplies tightened. The cow carcass market followed the trend of the boneless beef market and traded lower for the week.

The cow cuts market traded uneven. The 100% lean items traded sharply higher again on moderate demand for light offerings. The knuckles, chuck tenders and ribeye rolls traded weak to lower on moderate offerings and light demand.

Utility carcasses 1.00 lower; Cutter 1.00-2.00 lower; 90% boneless beef 4.50-6.00 lower; 85% 5.00 lower; 75% weak; 65% 1.00-2.50 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, April 03, 1997 was estimated at 81.56 per cwt., dn 3.11 from a week ago Friday.
